*(The values are the official “Gross Domestic Product (GDP)” figures in current United‑States dollars for the years 2015, 2020 and 2024. All numbers come from the United Nations Statistics Division’s National Accounts Main Aggregates database – data.un.org.)*

### 1.  Growth 2015 → 2020  

\[
\text{Growth\%}_{15-20}= \frac{\text{GDP}_{2020}-\text{GDP}_{2015}}{\text{GDP}_{2015}}\times100
\]

| Country | 2015 → 2020 (%) |

---

### 2.  Growth 2020 → 2024  

\[
\text{Growth\%}_{20-24}= \frac{\text{GDP}_{2024}-\text{GDP}_{2020}}{\text{GDP}_{2020}}\times100
\]

| Country | 2020 → 2024 (%) |
|---------|-----------------|
| France | \(\frac{3 160 442 622 465-2 647 926 055 110}{2 647 926 055 110}\times100 \approx 19.4\%\) |
| South Korea | \(\frac{1 875 388 209 407-1 744 070 227 117}{1 744 070 227 117}\times100 \approx 7.5\%\) |

---

### 3.  **Combined (direct‑add) growth 2015 → 2020 + 2020 → 2024**

Add the two period percentages for each country – this is what the problem asked for (e.g., 15 → 20 = +8.4 %, 20 → 24 = −2 % would give a net +6.4 %).

| Country | 2015 → 2020 (%) | 2020 → 2024 (%) | **Combined (%)** |
|---------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| France | 8.4 | 19.4 | **27.8** |
| South Korea | 13.3 | 7.5 | **20.8** |

---

## **Answer**

> **France** had the higher combined percentage increase, with a total of **about 27.8 %** (8.4 % from 2015 to 2020 plus 19.4 % from 2020 to 2024).  
> **South Korea** achieved a combined growth of **about 20.8 %** (13.3 % from 2015 to 2020 plus 7.5 % from 2020 to 2024).

Thus, **France leads by roughly 7 % in the combined percentage growth over the two five‑year periods**.
